questions.question: How much shorter was the bouncing-with-spray (BWS) residence time than the traditional retraction-bouncing mode?

options.D: It was equal within the reported comparison

questions.rationale: The conclusion quantifies the reduction as roughly 40%.
questions.evidence_quote: the reduced residence time compared with that of the retraction-bouncing mode is about 40%.

questions.question: What event initiates the shortened residence time in the BWS mode?

options.A: Vapor bubbles burst in the liquid film, creating holes from which the film recoils
options.B: The droplet freezes at the contact line
options.C: The substrate roughness ejects the entire droplet before spreading
options.D: A Leidenfrost vapor layer prevents all liquid recoil

questions.rationale: The proposed mechanism is bubble bursting, film perforation, and recoiling from the holes.
questions.evidence_quote: The reduction in the residence time is due to the burst of vapor bubbles formed in the liquid ﬁlm

questions.question: How did the authors operationally define droplet residence time in their heated-surface experiments?

options.A: From first visible contact with the substrate until visible detachment
options.B: From maximum spreading until the last satellite droplet evaporates
options.C: From impact until the first bubble bursts
options.D: From first thermal contact until the droplet reaches saturation temperature

questions.rationale: Their image-based definition uses the visible contact and detachment moments.
questions.evidence_quote: the moments that the droplet visually contacts the substrate and that it visually detaches the substrate.

questions.question: At the critical transition between RB and BWS modes, what size comparison is assumed for the vapor bubble?

options.A: Bubble radius rv is approximately the minimum liquid-film thickness bmin
options.B: Bubble diameter equals the initial droplet diameter D0
options.C: Bubble radius equals the maximum spread radius Rmax
options.D: Bubble radius is much smaller than bmin

questions.rationale: The model identifies bubble/film-thickness equality as the threshold for hole formation.
questions.evidence_quote: the radius of the vapor bubble is approximately equal to the minimum thickness of the ﬁlm

questions.question: What scaling for the minimum liquid-film thickness enters the model?
questions.rationale: Equation (4), cited from prior work, gives the Reynolds-number scaling.

questions.question: How is the maximum spreading radius related to Weber number in the film-boiling data?
questions.rationale: The measured spreading exponent is n=0.35 for this study.

questions.question: What transition-boundary scaling did the authors derive for a fixed liquid and initial droplet size?

options.D: ΔT is independent of impact speed

questions.rationale: After fixing the liquid and drop size parameters, the dimensionless relation reduces to this scaling.

questions.question: Under what condition did the authors treat the heat-transfer area A as constant in the scaling analysis?

options.A: For different liquids, A was assumed constant; comparison then fixes liquid and initial droplet size
options.B: A was fixed across every possible impact speed and all surfaces
options.C: A was set equal to the full wafer area
options.D: A was calculated from the number of vapor bubbles

questions.rationale: They assume A is constant across liquid comparisons, and then explain the same-liquid/same-size case.
questions.evidence_quote: For diﬀerent kinds of liquids, we suppose that the heat transfer area to the vapor bubble A can be regarded as a constant.

questions.question: Why does the critical Weber number increase with substrate temperature in the transition-boiling regime in the authors' explanation?

options.A: The vapor bubble becomes smaller for the considered time, so a thinner film (larger We) is needed for bursting
options.B: The droplet viscosity falls until the liquid film cannot spread
options.C: The maximum spread radius decreases as We rises
options.D: The bubble lifetime becomes infinite at higher temperature

questions.rationale: Their model attributes the threshold trend to reduced bubble size and the need for a thinner film to satisfy rv∼bmin.
questions.evidence_quote: it requires a thinner liquid ﬁlm (a larger We) for the threshold of the burst of the vapor bubble

questions.question: What limitation/future-work need do the authors identify for testing the BWS mechanism more directly?

options.A: Detailed numerical simulations and experimental measurements of the bursting bubbles are needed
options.B: The mechanism cannot be studied with high-speed imaging
options.C: Further work must replace all water-based liquids with metals
options.D: Only changing substrate roughness can test the theory

questions.rationale: The conclusion names direct bubble-resolved numerical and experimental work as helpful.
questions.evidence_quote: detailed numerical simulations and experimental measurements of the bursting bubbles
